_comment:
Derived by measuring 200 APIGen-MT-5k customer-service conversations, not by choosing convenient entities.

The result was uncomfortable and worth stating plainly. In this domain 82-99% of every mutable entity's mentions live in tool output rather than in speech: reservation ids are 83% machine output, airport codes 82%, payment methods 99%. The read path is forbidden to infer state from machine output -- that rule exists because a grep listing is not a statement about intent, and it was measured on the coding corpus. So a pattern-based tracker can only ever see the small remainder, and that is a property of the problem rather than a defect in the tracker.

What remains reachable is cabin class: 2,439 spoken mentions across 200 conversations, and in 41% of the conversations it takes more than one value. A user says they are in economy, then upgrades, then changes their mind about the upgrade. That is the last-write-wins case this library exists for, in a domain with no file paths in it at all.

The patterns require a natural-language construction, which is also what keeps them off the JSON tool payloads: `{"cabin": "economy"}` has no 'class' in it, so it cannot match. This is the same discipline as the coding schema -- require a phrasing, never a bare token.

Two defects were found by reading the registering turns, and both are worth
recording because neither was visible in any aggregate number:

1. "reservation ID corresponds" was extracted as `active_reservation = "corres"`.
   The pattern had no trailing word boundary, so it took six characters of a
   thirteen-letter word, and because every pattern is compiled case-insensitively
   an all-lowercase fragment satisfied an uppercase-id class. The id group is now
   case-scoped with (?-i:...) and closed with \b.

2. "basic economy" was extracted as `economy`. This domain distinguishes them --
   the policy prompt prices checked bags differently for a basic economy
   passenger than for an economy passenger, and the phrase appears 435 times in
   60 conversations -- so collapsing the two produces a confidently wrong value
   precisely when it matters. "basic economy" is now its own value.

3. A flight-options menu was read as a booking. One turn listed every cabin with
   its seat count and price and then asked the user which they wanted; the
   pattern took `Basic Economy` off the price list and recorded it as the
   passenger's cabin. The two fixed-width lookbehinds exclude the catalogue
   shape, which is the only place in this domain where a bare cabin name is an
   option rather than a statement. Naming it here because the fix is a pair of
   literal strings, which is the kind of thing that rots silently.

value_contracts.corpus_note: read_path_* counts what the read path can see: customer and agent turns, minus tool output and minus an agent turn listing its options; in_tool_output is what those exclusions cost
